heading: INT. MILLINERY SHOP - OAK STREET - 1924 - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. MILLINERY SHOP - OAK STREET - 1924 - AFTERNOON
A narrow shop of cut velvet and hatboxes stacked to the ceiling.
Dusty sun through the front window.
A bell hangs over the door, its clapper tied with ribbon.
MRS. EUGENIA PRATT, 50, proprietress, stands behind the counter in a black dress with a cameo at the throat.
She is severe and small and perfectly straight.
Beside her, her younger sister CORDELIA, 40, soft-faced, clutches a pincushion like a rosary.
At the door, a boy in a delivery cap, ALOYSIUS, 12, stands with an envelope.
He keeps one foot on the sill.
Telegram for Mrs. Pratt.
units.name: ALOYSIUS

units.text: Set it down.
units.name: EUGENIA

units.text: Set it down.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: They say it together, then glance at each other.
Set it down. ^CORDELIA Don't open it.
units.name: EUGENIA

units.text: Aloysius sets it down on the counter and retreats a step.
He watches the sisters as if they might spring.
Eugenia does not touch the envelope.
She turns her cameo a quarter turn, very slowly.
Cordelia takes a pin from the cushion and puts it back.
Is there a reply?
units.name: ALOYSIUS

units.text: No.
units.name: EUGENIA

units.text: She slides a coin across the wood.
He takes it and leaves, the ribbon-tied bell never ringing.
Cordelia lays a hand on the envelope.
Eugenia slides it out from under.
Neither looks at it.
Both look at the window.
